items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid affairs scandal
items.feedTitle: What Huang's resignation mean for chipmakers, AI and U.S. national security
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after admitting to an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, plus a second affair with an Nvidia executive. Colette Kress, the company's CFO, will serve as interim CEO. The resignation has triggered congressional investigations and raised national security concerns about AI chip exports to China and Nvidia's governance.

items.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills eight, including two children
items.feedTitle: New York building collapse kills 8, including 2 children
items.summary: A three-story apartment building in Brooklyn collapsed Wednesday, killing at least eight people including two children and injuring dozens more. First responders ended their search for additional survivors at the site. The collapse has prompted investigations into the building's structural integrity and safety compliance.

items.title: Trump warns of migrant caravans crossing Mexico border
items.feedTitle: Trump reverts to an old theme, warns of immigrant caravans
items.summary: President Trump revived warnings about migrant caravans moving through Mexico toward the US border in recent statements. Mexican President Sheinbaum disputed the characterization, saying no caravans have actually reached the US. The rhetoric reflects Trump's longstanding immigration focus amid broader policy discussions.

items.title: Senators probe RFK Jr. over Samoa trip testimony discrepancies
items.feedTitle: Senators probe RFK Jr.'s reason for Samoa trip after letter refuting his testimony published
items.summary: Democratic senators are investigating whether Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. lied to Congress about his reason for a 2019 trip to Samoa. The AP and The Guardian published documents in August that contradicted his earlier testimony. The probe raises questions about his candor and fitness for office.

items.title: Tornado spotted in Burlington County, New Jersey area
items.feedTitle: Tornado Spotted In Burlington County
items.summary: A tornado was spotted in Burlington County, New Jersey during powerful storms that swept the Philadelphia region. The storms produced significant hail and tornado damage across Delaware and New Jersey. A helicopter was damaged during the incident.

stlouis.title: Two students, teacher stabbed at Warrenton middle school
stlouis.feedTitle: 2 students, teacher injured in stabbing at Black Hawk Middle School, student in custody
stlouis.summary: Two students and a teacher were injured in a stabbing incident at Black Hawk Middle School in Warrenton. A student was taken into custody in connection with the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety in the St. Louis metro area.

stlouis.title: St. Louis school board votes to close nine schools
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis school board votes to close 9 schools - K-12 Dive
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis school board voted to close nine schools as part of budget and operational restructuring. The closures reflect ongoing challenges in the district's financial management and enrollment trends.

stlouis.title: Two-year-old dies in south St. Louis house fire
stlouis.feedTitle: 2-year-old girl dies in south St. Louis house fire without utilities, leading to push on available assistance resources
stlouis.summary: A 2-year-old girl died in a house fire in south St. Louis that occurred at a residence without utilities. The incident has prompted discussions about available assistance resources for families in need. Officials are investigating the circumstances of the fire.

items.title: US envoys meet Putin, say Europe will join Ukraine peace talks
items.feedTitle: After meeting Putin, U.S. envoys say Europe to join talks on ending Ukraine war
items.summary: US envoys meeting with Russian President Putin say European countries will have a voice in talks aimed at ending the Ukraine war. Putin took a hardline stance, saying Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine. The discussions mark an effort to include European allies in ongoing peace negotiations.

items.title: Microsoft global outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot
items.feedTitle: Microsoft begins restoring services as global outage affects Outlook and Teams
items.summary: Microsoft experienced a major global outage affecting nearly 130,000 users, disrupting Outlook email, Teams, Copilot, and other services for more than five hours on Thursday. The company said it was working to restore services and did not initially specify the cause of the disruption.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia, UNSC extends sanctions
items.feedTitle: Yemen’s Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctions
items.summary: Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted suspected Houthi drones and missiles targeting oil and military infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. The UN Security Council extended sanctions on Yemen through 2027 amid the renewed strikes. The escalation reflects ongoing regional tensions in the Strait of Hormuz area.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaker into turmoil
items.feedTitle: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one allegedly with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. His departure has prompted US lawmakers to question whether the relationship posed national security risks. The scandal has raised concerns about Nvidia's governance and its role in US-China tech competition.

items.title: PM Modi inaugurates Namma Metro Pink Line in Bengaluru
items.feedTitle: PM Modi in Bengaluru for Namma Metro Pink Line inauguration| Traffic diversions in city on November 13
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi visited Bengaluru on November 13 to inaugurate the partial opening of the Namma Metro Pink Line. The elevated section opening is expected to provide limited relief to the city's traffic congestion, with the crucial underground central business district section still pending completion. The project reflects India's continued infrastructure expansion efforts.

items.title: Activist Sonam Wangchuk under restrictions in Ladakh
items.feedTitle: Wangchuk under ‘house arrest’ as Ladakh rallies against hill council polls in winter
items.summary: Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk says he is under arbitrary restrictions by the administration, being kept at his residence and prevented from leaving. Wangchuk and other leaders have sought PM Modi's intervention over winter polls and warned of agitation if the government proceeds with elections during harsh winter conditions.

items.title: India bypasses own rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tech
items.feedTitle: India bypasses own rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tech
items.summary: India has bypassed its own procurement rules to purchase Cellebrite, Israeli phone-hacking technology, according to reports. The Home Minister signed off on the acquisition before standard evaluation processes, raising questions about oversight and accountability in the purchase of sensitive surveillance equipment.

items.title: IIT Kharagpur launches postgraduate medical programs
items.feedTitle: India’s oldest IIT is entering medical education. Here’s what will change
items.summary: IIT Kharagpur has become the first IIT to offer postgraduate medical programs, receiving approval from the National Medical Commission. The initiative marks the institution's entry into medical education and reflects India's efforts to expand quality medical training across premier technical institutes.

items.title: Government plans special session to clear Delimitation Bill
items.feedTitle: Government planning special Session to clear Delimitation Bill; Congress calls it a ‘bluster’
items.summary: The Indian government is planning a special parliamentary session to clear the Delimitation Bill, which would redraw electoral boundaries. Congress has criticized the move as a 'bluster,' calling it an attempt to 'manipulate' parties. The bill also includes a women's quota provision that remains contentious.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending H-1B deference rule; comment period closes Nov 13
immigration.feedTitle: DHS wants every H-1B extension reviewed from scratch; the rule is only proposed and comments close November 13
immigration.summary: DHS has proposed a rule to end USCIS deference to prior approvals on H-1B visa extensions, requiring each renewal to be reviewed from scratch. The proposed rule, still in comment period through November 13, could affect approximately 208,000 work visa renewals annually and potentially trigger 6,000 additional requests for evidence. This is a proposed rule, not yet finalized; comments are still being accepted.

immigration.title: IBM ends H-1B and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
immigration.feedTitle: IBM to end H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles amid Trump's immigration crackdown — Report
immigration.summary: IBM announced it will end H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting positions by the end of 2026, reportedly in response to Trump administration immigration restrictions. The move affects IBM's Consulting division and is likely to impact Indian IT workers who rely on these visa programs. This reflects broader corporate retreat from visa sponsorship amid tightening policy.

immigration.title: US revokes over 6,000 visas linked to birth tourism
immigration.feedTitle: US revokes over 6,000 visas linked to birth tourism, State Department says | Hindustan Times
immigration.summary: The State Department says it has revoked over 6,000 visas linked to birth tourism, implementing a new visa restriction policy targeting those who engage in or facilitate birth tourism. This is a finalized and in effect policy announced by the Trump administration as part of its effort to tighten visa controls.

items.feedTitle: GIFT Nifty falls 70 pts, signals weak start for Sensex, Nifty despite Asian markets rally; Nvidia crisis...
items.summary: GIFT Nifty futures fell 70 points on November 13, signaling a weak opening for Indian equities despite broader Asian market rallies. The decline reflects concerns about the Nvidia crisis and global volatility. Indian markets have been supported by FII inflows and lower oil prices in recent sessions.

items.title: Oil prices fall to lowest since August on Iran war comments
items.feedTitle: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’
items.summary: Oil prices fell to their lowest level since late August, with Brent crude dropping below $90 per barrel, after Trump said the war with Iran is 'effectively over.' The decline reflects reduced geopolitical risk premium and has supported broader market sentiment. Lower energy costs are helping ease inflation pressures globally.

items.title: SpaceX and Tesla merger talks progress, Bloomberg reports
items.feedTitle: SpaceX, Tesla merger talks progress, Bloomberg News reports
items.summary: Bloomberg News reports that talks between SpaceX and Tesla on a potential merger are progressing. Such a combination would represent one of the largest corporate mergers involving Elon Musk's companies. Details on valuation and timing remain unclear.

items.title: US home sales hit 16-year low in October amid high mortgage rates
items.feedTitle: Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid record-high mortgage rates
items.summary: Existing home sales in the US fell to 3.75 million units in October, down 8.8% year-over-year and marking the lowest level since 2010. Mortgage rates remained near three-year highs, depressing buyer demand. High prices and elevated borrowing costs are keeping many potential homebuyers out of the market.

cards.title: Admitting error before accusation defuses blame
cards.insight: Jensen Huang's partial admission (acknowledging one affair while others emerged) was too little and too late—the scandal metastasized because he appeared to hide instead of disclose. By contrast, transparent early disclosure of mistakes or conflicts reframes the narrative from 'caught' to 'honest,' shifting audience perception from distrust to forgiveness.
cards.takeaway: When vulnerable to criticism, volunteer damaging information yourself, frame it clearly, and move fast. Let others learn about your mistake from you, not from investigators or rivals.

cards.title: Authority alone doesn't survive scandal; character must precede crisis
cards.insight: Huang's technical genius and industry standing initially insulated him—until the spy affair threat made his credibility a liability, not an asset. High status accelerates a fall when personal judgment is questioned. The reverse is true: leaders who invest in consistent, modest behavior build reserves of goodwill that survive isolated lapses.
cards.takeaway: Build reputation through small, unglamorous acts of integrity over time. When crisis hits, that reservoir absorbs the blow; panic resignations are what people remember, not the talent.

cards.title: Distraction narratives fail when the core claim is existential
cards.insight: Trump's effort to redirect Vance away from Iran negotiations, or Newsom's commutation rollout—both assume the audience will accept a pivot. But when a message threatens identity or security (Huang as potential security risk), no deflection works. Audiences filter competing claims through the lens of what matters most.
cards.takeaway: Don't compete on secondary narratives when the primary concern is existential safety or trust. Acknowledge the existential claim first, address it directly, then redirect.

cards.title: Silence or slowness reads as complicity in an information vacuum
cards.insight: The Huang story exploded not because he had an affair, but because documents and rival allegations surfaced faster than his team's responses. Lawmakers and media filled the void with worst-case interpretations. Speed of response matters more than perfection; even a partial, honest statement early absorbs some outrage and slows narrative hardening.
cards.takeaway: In a crisis with reputational stakes, respond within 24 hours even if incomplete. Silence is interpreted as cover-up. A clear 'we're investigating and will update you' buys credibility; no comment buys suspicion.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO reportedly six times oversubscribed ahead of launch
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic's IPO is about six times oversubscribed, Bloomberg News reports
ai.summary: Anthropic's initial public offering is reportedly six times oversubscribed, indicating strong investor demand for the standalone frontier AI company. The IPO will test Wall Street's appetite for AI-focused businesses amid market volatility from the Nvidia scandal. Anthropic's Claude model has topped AI rankings as OpenAI limits access to some models.

ai.title: Nonprofits sue AI giants to freeze frontier model development
ai.feedTitle: Nonprofits sue Anthropic, Google, and other tech giants to freeze the AI arms race
ai.summary: California-based nonprofits have sued Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and other tech giants seeking to halt the development of advanced AI models, alleging the companies cannot adequately control their own technology. The lawsuit argues that frontier AI model training poses catastrophic risks and demands a freeze on such development. This is one of several legal efforts to impose regulatory constraints on rapid AI advancement.

ai.title: Google upgrades Gemini model for complex question comprehension
ai.feedTitle: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
ai.summary: Google has released an upgraded Gemini model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, designed to better understand complicated questions and deliver richer visual responses. The new version is now the cheapest and fastest model in performance benchmarks, offering 2.5x faster response times. The upgrade reflects intensifying competition in the frontier AI space following Nvidia's leadership turmoil.
